proofUses.reason: Keep the two-arm event intact after splitting at the three-terminal median; invariant counting and BK give the finite upper bound.
The increment uses edge-disjoint path witnesses, retains diagonal counts, and distinguishes a bridge from an edge inside a cluster.
Finite-product differentiation of cluster-functional densities, with the closed-edge factor and both unordered-edge normalization factors explicit.
BK bounds both weighted two-cluster deficits; differentiation of S divided by susceptibility squared retains the cycle contribution.
A definition; the remarks after it (implies connection, increasing, the triangle example) are immediate and invoke no other wiki assertion.
The identity is a group change of variables; the upper bound applies finite-coordinate BK (BNY8) to each summand and extends it to countably many bonds by finite-witness approximation.
The small-field limit is a union bound and inclusion-exclusion; the comparison uses the single-field first-moment limit (8B62) and the counting identity and BK bound of RIRJ.
The path transfer splits witnesses along the fixed path and applies Harris (X5SS) to the all-open path event and the separated-root event; the second bound is a direct union bound.

Small intensities use the row-sum susceptibility bound (53Z9) and the two-ghost bound of I6SP; large intensities apply the separated-root hypothesis along a short-edge path and the finite-path transfer of I6SP.
The proof is an l2/convolution estimate (Cauchy-Schwarz and finite truncation); the remarks applying it to Q6FI and 32MY come after the proof and are not used in it.
The proof is a finite enumeration of bond and mark assignments on the three-vertex star and invokes no other wiki assertion.
The proof splits a simple path to a marked vertex at z and applies finite-coordinate BK (BNY8), with increasing approximation on a countable graph, then a union bound.
On a finite graph the deletion bound and the three-branch decomposition each apply BK (BNY8); the countable case follows by exhaustion and dominated convergence.
The proof applies the distinct-cluster bound DTVY and then BK on Z^d (JRCI) with a union bound to discard field connections ending inside the box.
